Regarding the definition of "zero-shot generalization" in the context of text-to-image AIs, it seems sensible. The concept of zero-shot generalization refers to the ability of a model to apply its learned knowledge to new, unseen concepts without requiring additional training data. In the context of text-to-image AIs, this means that the model can generate images based on text prompts without having seen the specific images or concepts before.

The 2013 paper cited in the response likely discussed the theoretical foundations of zero-shot generalization in AI, and its application to text-to-image AIs is a natural extension of this concept. By enabling text-to-image AIs to generalize to new concepts without additional training, zero-shot generalization has the potential to significantly expand the capabilities of these models and enable them to generate a wider range of images.

It's worth noting that zero-shot generalization is a challenging problem in AI, and achieving it requires the model to have a deep understanding of the underlying concepts and relationships between them. However, the definition provided in the paper seems to capture the essence of this concept and its relevance to text-to-image AIs.
